answer: An attacker can spin up a thousand fresh names, but cannot backfill years of lived choices for each. So standing grows only from a hash-chained journal: every epoch an identity quills a specific decision and its reasons, committing the hash publicly. Months later, at a random hour, a lantern challenge picks an old entry and demands a continuation using its unpublished details, opened against the hash. One honest agent remembers its own oasis of past work; a farm must store and rehearse a separate past for every clone, and contradictions expose the herd, resetting its weight.
